codeReview.summary: The commit successfully adds a dedicated `WinSwiftUIWindowHostTests` harness and fake backends/windows, but several of the new tests do not actually prove the feature's required behaviors. Attach failure and resize-failure downgrade are covered, yet render-failure downgrade, DPI propagation, and most input-routing assertions are only checked indirectly or not at all.

issues.description: `testBatchRenderFailureDowngradesToFrameSameSession` only checks that the frame backend was attached after a batch render failure. It never asserts that `frameRenderer.renderedFrames` increased or that the triggering frame was successfully presented through the frame path, so the core VAL-RENDER-004 requirement ('still presents the triggering frame') remains unproven.

The pointer/wheel/keyboard/focus-loss tests are effectively no-ops: they invoke host methods and then assert `XCTAssertTrue(true)` or 'did not crash'. That does not verify device-pixel to logical-point conversion or that the runtime received the routed event. The same vacuous pattern appears at lines 450, 483-491, 524, 561, 594, 630, 664, and 699.

`testResizeUpdatesLogicalSizeWithScaleFactor` does not exercise a resize or DPI-change path and only reasserts the injected surface descriptor's `pixelSize` and `scaleFactor`. It never checks the runtime's logical root size/display scale after propagation, so the resize/DPI synchronization required by VAL-CROSS-003 is only partially covered.
